startersHint: Tap one to fill the box, then change the words to your own. You can also paste your script.
scriptLabel: Your captions, one line for each caption
scriptPlaceholder: Write one short line for each caption
scriptHint: Keep each line short, about 3 to 8 words, so it is easy to read. A new line means a new caption.
helpItems: Add your audio or video file. The sound is only played and read on your device. If a video file does not load, add its sound as an MP3 or M4A instead.
Tap Start. The sound plays. Each time a new line begins in the audio, tap the big button, or press the Space key.
Tapped the wrong time? Tap Undo and it goes back a little so you can tap again. You can also change any time later with the plus and minus buttons.
Save the SRT file and import it in CapCut, YouTube or Instagram Edits. You type the words, so names and Hindi words are always right.
soundHint: Add a voice note, a song, or a video file. Or choose No audio to tap along to a video you play on another device.
soundNone: No audio. A timer runs while you tap, then you set the end by tapping Stop.
audioFailed: That file could not be read. Try an MP3, M4A, WAV or OGG file.
tapReady: Press Start, then tap each time a caption should appear.
tapDone: All captions are timed. Tap Stop when the audio ends.
needLines: Write at least one line above first.
timesHint: Each caption starts at the time shown. Use the minus and plus buttons to move one by a tenth of a second. A caption without a tapped time follows the one before it.
timeOf: Start time of caption {n} in seconds
more: More options: tap delay and how long captions stay
shiftHint: People tap a little after they hear a line begin. This moves every caption earlier by this much. 0.2 seconds suits most people.
holdHint: Choose a time if you want the screen to go empty between captions.
notSaved: Your audio is not saved between visits, only your words and settings. Save your files before you leave the page.
